deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts with conformance testing
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Runtime foundational components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, JVM and JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm according to the proposal.
Scalus components are embedded in MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The proposal states Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js receives over 20,000 downloads per month.
The resubmission reduces the prior proposal from ₳8,503,000 over 12 months to about ₳2,464,844 over 9 months, removes contingency, and reduces FTE from 8.25 to 2.25.
The funded scope excludes a standalone production-grade JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
Delivery is proposed as three quarterly milestones from July 2026 through March 2027 with maintenance running continuously across all milestones.
The proposal says delivery will be milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr Engineering says every prior Scalus milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, emphasizing maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with a reduced budget and scope compared with a prior proposal.
